values: Device kinds (sensing device, actuating device) are subclasses of ssn:Device; Patient is both an Actor and a FeatureOfInterest subclass.
The data are modelled with SAREF, not SOSA/SSN: every saref:Measurement links to the same Device, FeatureOfInterest, Property and UnitOfMeasurement entities.
sosa:Observation is declared equivalent to the work's own class lhr:EnvSSNResource, used to integrate SOSA data with FHIR health resources.
Measurements are not observations: signal properties (ev:ActivePower, ev:SoC) attach external time-series signals directly to the hosted devices, queried with SigSPARQL.
Kinds of ICT equipment are classes grouped under giri:System, a subclass of sosa:System; observations feed the work's own metric instances (girc:Metric).
Observations are kept in a time-series database in tabular form and mapped to SOSA; KPIs come from the EM-KPI ontology.
Unit and observed property are not on the observation but on the sosa:ObservationCollection that contains it (factorisation).
Own System, Sensor and Actuator classes subclass the SOSA ones; system and state conditions are subclasses of sosa:Condition (SSN).
Observations as blank nodes, one per RDF message; sosa:resultTime proposed to define the version order of messages.
SWRL rules over sosa:madeObservation and observation names derive privacy policies and consent requests; the observation carries its own observation_name and data category.
Observations subclassed into NumericObservation (hasSimpleResult) and StatusObservation (hasStatus to a Status individual); only selected SOSA properties are imported, not the SOSA classes.
KnowWhereGraph-Lite collapses the SOSA observation kernel into one predicate per observed property and result time (e.g. averageHeatingDegreeDaysPerMonthAug2021) pointing directly to the value.
Own properties link SOSA sensors to the rest: isObservedBy (actor to sosa:Sensor) and sendDatato (sosa:Sensor to the work's Data class) instead of observations.
Sensors and observable properties are related spatially to bridge components (BRCOMP) and spaces (SPOT) for component-based queries.
Uses the 2011 SSN (ssnx) with DOLCE UltraLite; a measurement observation has parts that are the per-phenomenon observations.

Observations subclassed by modality (TimeSeriesObservation, ImageObservation, ComputedObservation); DetectionMethod subclasses sosa:Procedure; SWRL rules compare hasSimpleResult with specification limits bound to the same observable property.
Humans doing field surveys or posting volunteered geographic information are treated as sensors; wetland classes reuse ENVO.
Attributes of grid cells are modelled as observations; grid features related by RCC8 spatial relations.
qb:Observation (RDF Data Cube) declared equivalent to sosa:Observation, so water-quality cube observations are SOSA observations; O&M SamplingPoint made a subclass of geosparql:Point.
Social media postings are modelled as observations of social sensors (resultTime, senso:isReportingOn a string) and matched to observable properties by NLP similarity.
MAPF agents (ma:Agent) are aligned with sosa:Platform, with agent states carrying location and time.
Measurements are modelled with SAREF (saref:Measurement), compared with but not expressed as SOSA observations.
dcat:Dataset is declared a subclass of sosa:Result, so results stored in external files or databases are described by DCAT distributions or data services.

Only TBox axioms are shown: an own IoTDevice class hasSensor sosa:Sensor, ssn:System carries an ethic mode, and observed properties are evaluated with SEAS evaluations linked to sustainability metrics.
ssn:Property is used instead of sosa:ObservableProperty as the type of properties; the SSN Stimulus-Sensor-Observation and SOSA sampling patterns are added to a building ODP.
Observation classes defined by a threshold on the simple result (HighTempObservation); sosa:observes is used to give the sensor's unit (qudt:DegreeCelsius).
The manufacturer's normal output range is modelled as ssn-system:SystemCapability with a MeasurementRange to detect sensor faults; robot paths are procedures linked to sensors by ssn:implements.
No sosa:Observation: sosa:madeBySensor is put directly on a qudt:Quantity describing a data series, with qudt:standardUncertainty for metrological traceability.
Rules classify observations into own observation classes (ObservationToHighLevelEnergy, TrustedObservations) with a trust value.

The work relies on the distinction between the feature of interest (the sample) and the ultimate feature of interest to make datasets searchable across disciplines; AGROVOC and TAXREF-LD terms are preferred.
Stations, vehicles and charging equipment are modelled as subclasses of sosa:Sensor that register own record objects (uiot:SensorRecord) aggregating sosa:Observation and SKOS state concepts.
Observations are logged as strings or controlled-vocabulary concepts for invariant properties, and as instances (optionally following the sosa:Observation model) for time-varying ones.
Signals not produced by a sensor get a vss:VirtualSensor to stay compliant with the SOSA pattern; rules over observations build step:Episode instances of semantic trajectories.

Occupant feedback is modelled like an observation (Wearable gives Feedback on a Property of a FeatureOfInterest) with OFO's own terms aligned with SOSA; property chains infer feature of interest and location.
No observation node: sosa:hasSimpleResult is asserted on the sensor itself and the triple is annotated with a certainty value using RDF-star.
System and sensor properties (operating power range, response time, measurement range) describe the portable measurement system.
sosa:Procedure describes the steps by which an actuator changes the state of the world in context-aware responses.

Every VSS signal becomes a property class and every signal sensor or actuator a device class; virtual systems stand in for sensors where none is physical; trajectory episodes are labelled by rules over observations.
QUDT chosen as the vocabulary of units and quantities; how it is attached is not shown.
No observations: sensors and platforms (Sentinel-2) are prov:Agents associated with the activity that generated a dataset, described with DCAT and Data Cube (qb4st) structures.
Quantity-specific object properties (hasTemperature, hasPressure, hasHumidity…) and value properties are added instead of relying only on observedProperty and hasSimpleResult.
Zones and devices are both platforms (nested through sosa:hosts); quality indicators are attached to observations or sensors; devices carry a status and a coverage area history.

New relations are minted in the sosa namespace (sosa:close, sosa:hasSpatial, sosa:hasTemporal) by SWRL rules over sensors and observations; reconstructed values are a subclass of sosa:Observation; sensor ID and range via ssn:hasSystemProperty.

A MERODE conceptual model in which Device generalises sensor and actuator and Device Usage generalises observation, actuation and sampling, with a constraint that a usage concerns a single feature of interest.

Observations subclassed by theme (VulnerabilityObservation); census and survey data modelled as observations; observable properties modelled bottom-up from datasets and integration relies on space and time rather than properties.
Process-mining event logs are modelled as sosa:Result subclasses (Event) carrying case id, activity name and timestamp attributes.
Observations without sensor or property in the example stream, only a feature of interest (an oven or pizza identifier) and a QUDT result.
EP-Plan plans are aligned with SSN device descriptions by extending ssn:Procedure followed by an ssn:System.
Uses the 2011 SSN (ssnx); quality-of-observation attributes and values (qoo:hasQoO) are attached to observation values, and virtual sensors (web APIs) are described with SSN capabilities.
